messages:
sophia: Heads-up — product asked for a per-team 'explainable cost' card that shows delegated quota impact + cache savings. They want a simple line that says: 'You saved X tokens via cache, Y tokens billed due to quota delegation' and a tooltip explaining attribution.

mike: ugh the attribution part is the hairy one. delegated quotas mean we sometimes route to another tenant's warm cache. Do we credit the requester or the cache owner?

tara: product wants the requester to see the effective cost they paid (so show net token burn after any credits), but also an optional breakdown that identifies who actually got the cache savings for accounting.

lee: +1 on split view. For billing we need canonical owner = cache owner. For UX we can show "apparent savings" to the caller and a link to the allocation log. That keeps invoices accurate while giving devs the friendly number.

sophia: ok so UI shows two numbers: "Displayed cost" (what the app experienced) and "Allocated cost" (how our ledger will assign it). Tooltip explains differences.

mike: technical debate: do we compute allocated cost in the dashboard by replaying the router decisions or by calling the attribution service with the request id? Replaying is cheaper for dashboard sampling but can diverge from billing.

tara: we already have the attribution service (cost-allocator). I'd vote dashboard calls the allocator API with a sample of request_ids. We then cache results and surface them. That matches billing and avoids subtle mismatches.

lee: downside: allocator API is fragile and rate-limited. If we call for many rows it will OOM. We need a condensed endpoint: /v1/allocator/summary?range=&route_ids=&sample=100

mike: agreed — we can add a bulk summary endpoint that returns: {"request_count": "N", "apparent_tokens": "T", "allocated_tokens": "A", "cache_savings": "S"} per route. small JSON, cheap to compute because allocator can run on pre-aggregated logs.

sophia: can we include uncertainty bands? product likes the "~" notion when sampling. e.g. Displayed cost: 1.2k ± 5%.

tara: yep. allocator can return sample_size and margin estimate. We'll need consistent sampling keys for reproducibility.

mike: implementation note: we should not query live KV caches for every dashboard render. Use daily aggregates for historical ranges and live sampling for <24h with a cap. Also add a fallback to show estimator heuristic: heuristic = apparent - (prefetch_rate * avg_prefetch_saving). Show that if allocator timed out.

lee: onboarding UX: console should show a small "explain" modal with three lines: 1) what you pay, 2) who received the cache credit, 3) how confident we are. Also link to raw audit rows in the infra console.

sophia: privacy/security check — exposing cache owner IDs to product users might leak tenant info. We should only show anonymized team names or internal IDs when the viewer has billing role.

tara: good catch. we'll gate the detailed allocation column behind admin scope. Regular devs get aggregated/anon breakdowns.

mike: plan of attack: 1) add bulk allocator summary endpoint (backend) 2) add sampling + heuristic fallback (backend) 3) console: new card with two numbers + tooltip + explain modal + gated detail link (frontend) 4) e2e: make sure daily aggregates match billing window for invoices (ops).

lee: can we also show model/unit economics next to the cost card? e.g. model SKU, quantization profile, per-token marginal cost. product requested that as a small subline.

sophia: yes include model SKU and an index: "unit cost vs baseline". We'll surface quantization/variant and a link to recommend Optimize actions.

tara: FYI: costbot just posted the latest snapshot for 03/19 — overall prefetch hit rate changed ~2% which will affect the displayed savings. pinging team for awareness.

costbot: System: snapshot 2026-03-19T08:00Z: prefetch_hit_rate=18.7%, avg_prefetch_saving_per_hit=3.2 tokens, alloc_queue_len=2

mike: thanks costbot. I'll prototype the /bulk-allocator-summary endpoint and a fallback estimator. ETA EOW for a basic PoC.

sophia: awesome. tara/lee can you draft the console wire with the two-number UX and explain modal? we'll iterate after PoC.

tara: on it. will post a quick mock tomorrow.

lee: I'll draft the backend spec for the summary endpoint and the sampling contract in the next hour, will share.

sophia: sweet. if anyone sees edgecases (cross-tenant caches, model-variant fallbacks) drop them here so we can enumerate test cases.

mike: cross-tenant caches + fallback chains are the scary ones. I'll add a small matrix of attribution rules to the PR.

tara: thanks all :thumbsup:
